The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Large dark brown/black necrotic areas mainly at the margins and upper left portion
- Some yellowing (chlorosis) adjacent to the dark areas
- Irregular lesion borders
- Center of leaf still mostly green

Top candidates: Late_Blight, Early_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers. Let me check one reference from each.

The Late_Blight LeafNet_423 is a very strong visual match to the test image - dark brown/black necrosis on one side of the leaf with the rest remaining green. Let me check one more class before finalizing.

Gray Mold shows fruit rot - doesn't match the test image at all.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Reference | Match to test |
|-----------|--------------|
| Late_Blight/LeafNet_423 | **Excellent** - same dark brown/black marginal necrosis on portion of leaf, rest green, identical layout |
| Late_Blight/CDDM_498 | Good - large dark necrotic areas |
| Early_Blight | Poor - concentric target spots, different pattern |
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | Poor - many small circular spots |
| Alternaria | Not comparable (microscopic) |
| TSWV | Poor - whole plant wilting |
| Gray_Mold | Poor - fruit rot |

The test image closely matches Late Blight: irregular dark brown/black necrosis progressing from the leaf margin inward, with a clear boundary between dead and still-green tissue, and slight yellowing in the transition zone.
